links.comparator_used: AI binary diagnosis shown without a spatial display (GradCAM heatmap compared with binary feedback)
links.outcome: Radiographer agreement with AI feedback, trust in AI and decision switching
links.effect: Participants disagreed with heatmaps on abnormal examinations 45.8% of the time and agreed with binary feedback on 86.7% of examinations (26/30). Only 2 participants would decision switch in response to all AI feedback (0.7%). Participants agreed with the heatmap's localisation of pathology 22.2% of the time (n=32). Agreement correlated with trust for both formats, more strongly for GradCAM (-.515; -.584, large) than for binary (-.309; -.369, medium).
links.tradeoff: Heatmaps with imprecise localisation were often rejected, and trust depended on how accurate the localisation was. This creates a risk of reduced trust when the heatmap does not match the clinician's own reading.
links.quote: Participants disagreed with the AI heatmaps for the abnormal examinations 45.8% of the time and agreed with binary feedback on 86.7% of examinations (26/30 presentations).

design_hint: explainable AI feedback format (heatmaps vs binary output)
